analysis.title: US Market Intelligence | Afternoon Briefing (October 13, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed modestly lower and rangebound (SPX -0.0%, NDX -0.3%, RTY -0.4%). Decliners concentrated in Healthcare, Tech and Banks. Semis/memory extended the slide (SOXX -17bp, DRAM -3.4%) while money rotated into hyperscalers (META +2.7%, ORCL +4.3%).
Banks fell on day 1 of earnings despite in-line results and positive economic outlooks (C -5.6%, WFC -3.1%). Payments (MA, V) outperformed on card volume growth reported by large banks.
NY Fed President Williams was dovish: he sees no need for a rate hike in 2027. Rate-sensitive sectors (Housing, Retail) outperformed. CPI is released tomorrow (Oct 14, 8:30am ET).

Bank earnings macro read-through: consumer spending and credit remain strong, supported by the labor market. Card spending grew 10% y/y at JPM and 13% at C. Delinquencies and net credit losses fell y/y at C and WFC. Corporate credit is healthy at C (low non-accruals and net credit losses).
WFC says higher prices weigh on sentiment and lower-income households are more sensitive to financing costs, inflation and fuel, but that group is described as stable and not getting worse.

Chase spending data shows total September spending growth of 6.6% y/y, up from 5.3% in August. Upper-, middle- and lower-income cohorts grew 7.8%, 8.2% and 6.6%. Lower-, middle- and higher-income wage growth in August was 4.7%, 3.8% and 3.7%.

Mkt Intel stays bullish on the US consumer and sees Q3 earnings as a positive catalyst. The JPM Retail basket (JP2RTL) is down 8.7% from its August peak on affordability and rising yields. L/S ratio percentile since Jan 2018 is 37% for Retail and 38% for Consumer Discretionary (data as of Oct 8, 2025).

JPM financial specialist Rob O'Dwyer calls the bank selloff a head-scratcher, likely driven by quant and passive flow. He argues the flatter curve (2s10s 5bp flatter) does not matter much, since the front end (3m5y) is roughly unchanged, so he sees a reason to fade the move and buy the group. He also notes re-grossing into the print is a small technical headwind because fundamental funds have less capacity to add longs.

WFC guidance: 4Q NIM stable q/q, NII pace to increase in 4Q, C&I loan demand healthy, loan growth expected above mid-single-digit y/y in 4Q26, no broad-based credit deterioration. C's ROTCE comments disappointed, but O'Dwyer thinks C is sandbagging and expects FY ROTCE near 12%.

TMT desk (Heavey): AI/Semis lead lower but SMH is off its lows. AI-disruption baskets are bouncing and fears of agents replacing internet/e-commerce are fading for now. Flows show a flight to mega-cap quality, with META, MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN all buy names.

META moved its earnings date up a week to Wed 10/21, prompting speculation about an equity raise. Heavey says the fundamental backdrop is strong either way. Ruth Porat said GOOGL capex will be materially higher in 2027, and capex slowdown fears look overblown.

Healthcare desk (Bukzin): broad-based healthcare weakness with money rotating into TMT. JNJ was a crowded hedge fund long and its print was not enough. The desk is selling biotech (INCY, COGT) and buying distributors, and sees generalist demand for BSX for the first time in a while. Med tech is a show-me quarter but sets up for a tactical trade given tax-loss supply and seasonality.

Financials desk (Barry): V +9.4% MTD and MA +8.9% MTD. Bank card volume vs 2Q: JPM decelerated 40bp, WFC accelerated 10bp, C accelerated 60bp to 13%. All beat Street estimates for V/MA US volume decelerating 100bp, and JPM's own spending preview of 80bp deceleration.

US Mkt Intel remains Tactically Bullish into earnings. Semis are about 20% below July lows and about 15% below June ATHs, which the desk calls an inflection point. Last week's OpenAI accounting misinterpretation caused a 3.4% decline Thursday. Breadth is deteriorating but could reverse into earnings.

Monetization menu (Oct 12) favors Tech and some Cyclicals with the AI theme globally bullish. The COVID Reopening theme should focus on Cruise Lines, Hotels and Retailers, given consumer strength and insulation from elevated energy prices. Internationally, ex-AI, the desk likes Brazil and Japan.
The market currently prices a December hike and two hikes in FY27. Dovish inflation prints could remove hike expectations and lower yields, which the desk lists as a catalyst.
Market levels: WTI +126bp at $94.92, NatGas $3.32, Gold $4,159, Silver $59.12, 10Y at 5.215%, VIX at 15.27.

earnings_insights: JPM (reported 10/13): debit and credit spend grew 10% y/y. Card net charge-off rate still expected at approximately 3.2%.

C (reported 10/13): spend volume up 13%, average loans up 9%, partly offset by declines in private label cards. Card net credit losses and delinquencies declined y/y. Corporate non-accrual loans and net credit losses remained low. Stock -5.6%.

WFC (reported 10/13): charge-off ratio down from 2Q and a year ago, early-stage delinquencies at historically low levels. Guides 4Q NIM stable q/q and loan growth above mid-single-digit y/y in 4Q26. Stock -3.1%.
JPM, WFC and C card volume growth was ahead of Street estimates that had V/MA US volume decelerating 100bp.
JNJ (reported 10/13): print was not enough for a crowded long and the med tech segment was underwhelming.
META moved its earnings date up one week to Wed 10/21.
Upcoming earnings: BAC, BLK, FAST, MS, PGR, STT on 10/14. AA, BNY, IBKR, JBHT, PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB on 10/15. CFG, TFC, TRV on 10/16.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks reported in-line earnings, strong consumer credit and a favorable loan outlook. The JPM specialist says the selloff looks driven by quant and passive flow and argues to fade it.
tension_points.bear_case: The curve is 5bp flatter, re-grossing into the print limits capacity for fundamental buyers to add longs, and C's ROTCE guidance disappointed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not stated explicitly, though a hotter CPI print or a steeper hike path would pressure the group.

tension_points.bull_case: The SOX is about 20% off its July lows and Hynix/Samsung earnings point to ongoing thematic strength. Breadth could reverse into earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Semis and memory extended the slide, with a 3-day losing streak after the OpenAI news and a tech unwind risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A tech earnings miss or momentum unwind would break the tactically bullish view.

tension_points.bull_case: Chase spending accelerated to +6.6% y/y, bank card volumes beat Street estimates and credit metrics are improving.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher prices weigh on sentiment and lower-income households are sensitive to financing costs, inflation and fuel.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker consumer data, or a deteriorating labor market, which WFC says would change the view.
